description: Everything under Photoshop's Filter menu: the large interactive workspaces (Filter Gallery, Camera Raw Filter, Liquify, Vanishing Point, Adaptive Wide Angle, Lens Correction, Blur Gallery and the AI-driven Neural Filters), plus the classic pixel filters grouped by submenu (Blur, Distort, Noise, Pixelate, Render, Sharpen, Stylize and Other). Most of these can be applied non-destructively as Smart Filters after Filter > Convert for Smart Filters, and many have an ExtendScript ArtLayer equivalent for batch automation.

tools.name: Filter Gallery
tools.description: Opens a large resizable preview window that hosts the Artistic, Brush Strokes, Sketch, Texture and the Filter Gallery members of the Distort and Stylize families (Diffuse Glow, Glass, Ocean Ripple, Glowing Edges). Effects can be stacked into an effect layer list, reordered, hidden and re-tuned before you commit, which is far faster than applying each filter separately. Use it for painterly, sketched, halftone or textured looks and for quickly auditioning combinations of creative effects.

parameters.name: Effect layer list
parameters.description: Stack of applied effects at the bottom right; drag to reorder, click the eye to hide, click the New Effect Layer icon to add another pass.

parameters.name: Artistic
parameters.description: Colored Pencil, Cutout, Dry Brush, Film Grain, Fresco, Neon Glow, Paint Daubs, Palette Knife, Plastic Wrap, Poster Edges, Rough Pastels, Smudge Stick, Sponge, Underpainting, Watercolor.

parameters.name: Brush Strokes
parameters.description: Accented Edges, Angled Strokes, Crosshatch, Dark Strokes, Ink Outlines, Spatter, Sprayed Strokes, Sumi-e.

parameters.name: Distort (gallery)
parameters.description: Diffuse Glow, Glass and Ocean Ripple - the three Distort filters that live inside the gallery rather than the Filter > Distort submenu.

parameters.name: Sketch
parameters.description: Bas Relief, Chalk & Charcoal, Charcoal, Chrome, Conte Crayon, Graphic Pen, Halftone Pattern, Note Paper, Photocopy, Plaster, Reticulation, Stamp, Torn Edges, Water Paper - most use the current foreground/background colors.

parameters.name: Stylize (gallery)
parameters.description: Glowing Edges, which finds color edges and adds a neon glow; the remaining Stylize filters live in Filter > Stylize.

parameters.name: Texture
parameters.description: Craquelure, Grain, Mosaic Tiles, Patchwork, Stained Glass, Texturizer.

parameters.name: Zoom / preview
parameters.description: Zoom controls under the preview pane; collapse the thumbnail browser with the arrow next to the OK button to enlarge the preview.

tools.example:
1. Choose Image > Mode > 8 Bits/Channel if the document is 16- or 32-bit.
2. Select the layer (or Filter > Convert for Smart Filters first, to stay editable).
3. Choose Filter > Filter Gallery...
4. Click a category thumbnail, e.g. Artistic > Dry Brush, and set Brush Size, Brush Detail and Texture.
5. Click the New Effect Layer icon and add Texture > Texturizer on top of it.
6. Drag the effect layers to change the order, then click OK.
tools.notes: Filter Gallery only runs on 8-bit RGB, Grayscale or Duotone-converted documents; it is greyed out in 16-bit, 32-bit, CMYK-only workflows and on Lab in some cases. Because the Sketch and several Texture filters use the foreground and background colors, set those before opening the gallery. Stack order matters - the bottom effect layer is applied first. There is no dedicated ExtendScript DOM method for the gallery; script it with an Action or executeAction descriptor instead.

tools.name: Convert for Smart Filters
tools.description: Converts the selected layer or layers into a Smart Object so that every filter applied afterwards is recorded as an editable Smart Filter beneath the layer in the Layers panel. Smart Filters keep their dialog settings, get their own blending options (mode and opacity) and share a single Smart Filter mask, so you can re-open, re-order, mask or delete an effect at any time without touching the original pixels. Use it as the first step of virtually any filter workflow you may want to revise later.
tools.usage: Filter > Convert for Smart Filters (equivalent to Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object)

parameters.name: Smart Filter mask
parameters.description: A single white mask attached to the filter stack; paint black on it to hide the filter locally.

parameters.name: Blending Options
parameters.description: Double-click the slider icon to the right of a Smart Filter name to set its blend mode and opacity (the equivalent of Edit > Fade for a normal filter).

parameters.name: Filter stack order
parameters.description: Drag Smart Filters up or down under the layer to change the order in which they are evaluated.

parameters.name: Visibility
parameters.description: Click the eye icon next to an individual Smart Filter to toggle it off without deleting it.

tools.notes: A locked Background layer must be unlocked (or duplicated) before it can be converted. Smart Filters cost extra memory and file size because the original layer data is embedded. Vanishing Point cannot be recorded as a Smart Filter. Applying a filter with the ArtLayer apply* methods to a Smart Object layer works only because Photoshop routes it through the Smart Filter machinery - a few filters still rasterize, so test your script.

tools.name: Adaptive Wide Angle
tools.description: Straightens lines that wide-angle, fisheye or stitched panoramic lenses have bent, using the lens profile embedded in the image metadata to build a correction model. You draw constraint lines along features that should be straight (horizons, building edges, poles) and Photoshop warps the image so those features become straight while keeping the rest of the geometry plausible. Use it for architecture shot with an ultra-wide lens and for cleaning up Photomerge panoramas that bow in the middle.

parameters.name: Correction
parameters.description: Projection model: Fisheye, Perspective, Auto or Full Spherical (use Full Spherical for 360-degree stitched panoramas with a 2:1 aspect ratio).

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Scales the corrected image up to hide the transparent wedges that the warp creates at the edges.

parameters.name: Focal Length / Crop Factor
parameters.description: Manual lens values, used when the file has no usable EXIF lens data.

parameters.name: Constraint tool (C)
parameters.description: Drag along a feature that should be straight; Shift-drag constrains it to strictly horizontal or vertical.

parameters.name: Polygon Constraint tool (Y)
parameters.description: Click four corners to define a quadrilateral (a window, a sign) that should become rectangular.

parameters.name: Move tool (M) / Hand (H) / Zoom (Z)
parameters.description: Reposition the image inside the frame and navigate the preview.

parameters.name: As Shot / Preview / Show Constraints / Show Mesh
parameters.description: Preview toggles for comparing the correction and inspecting the warp mesh.

tools.example:
1. Convert the layer with Filter > Convert for Smart Filters so the constraints stay editable.
2. Choose Filter > Adaptive Wide Angle...
3. Leave Correction on Auto if the lens profile was detected, otherwise pick Fisheye or Perspective and enter Focal Length and Crop Factor.
4. With the Constraint tool, drag along the horizon, then along a vertical building edge (hold Shift to lock it).
5. Raise Scale slightly to push the transparent corners out of frame and click OK.
6. Crop away any residual transparency.
tools.notes: Only works on 8- and 16-bit RGB or Grayscale documents. It needs a supported lens profile for the Auto and Fisheye models; without one the correction is purely manual. Do not confuse the shortcut with Camera Raw Filter (Shift+Ctrl+A) - Adaptive Wide Angle adds Alt/Opt. For simple barrel/pincushion distortion and chromatic aberration, Filter > Lens Correction is usually the better tool.

tools.name: Camera Raw Filter
tools.description: Opens the full Adobe Camera Raw editing environment as a filter so you can apply raw-style tonal, color, optical and local corrections to any rendered layer - JPEGs, scans, composites, even rasterized type. It brings the Basic, Curve, Detail, Color Mixer, Color Grading, Optics, Geometry, Effects and Calibration panels plus the AI masking tools (Select Subject, Select Sky, Select Objects, Select People) into Photoshop. Use it as a one-stop global grade, or as the most convenient way to apply the modern AI Lens Blur and film-grain/vignette effects.

parameters.name: Basic
parameters.description: White Balance (Temperature, Tint), Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks, Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vibrance, Saturation.

parameters.name: Curve
parameters.description: Parametric and Point tone curves, plus per-channel Red, Green and Blue curves.

parameters.name: Detail
parameters.description: Sharpening (Amount, Radius, Detail, Masking) and Noise Reduction (Luminance, Detail, Contrast, Color).

parameters.name: Color Mixer / Color Grading
parameters.description: HSL adjustment per color range, B&W mixing, and three-way shadow/midtone/highlight color wheels with Blending and Balance.

parameters.name: Optics
parameters.description: Remove Chromatic Aberration, Use Profile Corrections, Defringe and manual Distortion/Vignetting sliders.

parameters.name: Geometry
parameters.description: Upright modes (Auto, Level, Vertical, Full, Guided) and manual Vertical/Horizontal/Rotate/Aspect/Scale/Offset transforms.

parameters.name: Effects
parameters.description: Grain (Amount, Size, Roughness), Post-Crop Vignetting and, in Photoshop 25 and later, the AI-driven Lens Blur panel with an automatic depth map and Bokeh controls.

parameters.name: Masking
parameters.description: Subject, Sky, Background, Objects, People, Brush, Linear Gradient, Radial Gradient, Color Range, Luminance Range and Depth Range masks, each carrying the full slider set.

tools.example:
1. Select the layer and choose Filter > Convert for Smart Filters so the Camera Raw settings stay re-editable.
2. Choose Filter > Camera Raw Filter... (Shift+Ctrl+A).
3. In Basic, set Exposure, Contrast, Highlights/Shadows and add Texture or Dehaze.
4. Open Masking, click Select Sky, and pull Exposure down on the sky mask only.
5. In Optics, enable Remove Chromatic Aberration.
6. Click OK; double-click the Camera Raw Filter Smart Filter later to reopen the same settings.
tools.notes: Not available on 32-bit/channel documents (convert to 16-bit first) and not available on a layer mask or a single channel. The AI Denoise / Enhance command is only offered for genuine raw files opened in Camera Raw, not through the Camera Raw Filter. Applying it to a flattened pixel layer is destructive unless you convert to a Smart Object first.

tools.name: Lens Correction
tools.description: Fixes the common optical defects of a lens: barrel and pincushion distortion, chromatic aberration (color fringing) and corner vignetting, and additionally offers perspective and rotation transforms. Auto Correction applies a matching lens profile from the built-in database based on the camera and lens EXIF data; the Custom tab exposes the same corrections as manual sliders for scans and profileless images. Use it before any compositing or straightening work so the geometry you build on is already true.

parameters.name: Auto Correction > Correction
parameters.description: Checkboxes for Geometric Distortion, Chromatic Aberration, Vignette and Auto Scale Image.

parameters.name: Auto Correction > Edge
parameters.description: How to fill the areas the correction empties: Transparency, Edge Extension, Black Color or White Color.

parameters.name: Search Criteria
parameters.description: Camera Make, Camera Model and Lens Model used to pick a lens profile; profiles can also be loaded from Adobe Lens Profile Downloader.

parameters.name: Custom > Remove Distortion
parameters.description: Negative values correct pincushion, positive values correct barrel distortion.

parameters.name: Custom > Chromatic Aberration
parameters.description: Three fringe sliders: Fix Red/Cyan Fringe, Fix Green/Magenta Fringe, Fix Blue/Yellow Fringe.

parameters.name: Custom > Vignette
parameters.description: Amount (darken or lighten the corners) and Midpoint (how far toward the centre the effect reaches).

parameters.name: Custom > Transform
parameters.description: Vertical Perspective, Horizontal Perspective, Angle (rotation) and Scale.

parameters.name: Show Grid / Size / Color
parameters.description: Overlay grid used to judge straightness while correcting.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Convert for Smart Filters, then Filter > Lens Correction...
2. On the Auto Correction tab, confirm the detected Camera Make/Model/Lens, and tick Geometric Distortion, Chromatic Aberration and Vignette.
3. Set Edge to Edge Extension and tick Auto Scale Image.
4. Switch to Custom and nudge Vertical Perspective to square up the building.
5. Turn on Show Grid to check the verticals, then click OK.
tools.notes: Supports 8- and 16-bit documents; it is unavailable in 32-bit mode. If no lens profile is found, search online from the profile fly-out menu or correct manually on the Custom tab. Camera Raw Filter > Optics does the same job with more up-to-date profiles and is the better choice inside a Camera Raw based workflow.

tools.name: Liquify
tools.description: A dedicated warping workspace that lets you push, pull, rotate, pucker, bloat and reflect pixels with brush-based tools, backed by a deformation mesh you can freeze, thaw, reconstruct and save. Face-Aware Liquify detects faces and exposes named sliders for eyes, nose, mouth and face shape, which makes portrait retouching far more controllable than freehand warping. Use it for body and product reshaping, for fixing clothing and hair edges, and for wholly abstract liquid distortions.

parameters.name: Forward Warp (W)
parameters.description: Pushes pixels in the direction you drag - the main reshaping tool.

parameters.name: Reconstruct (R) / Smooth (E)
parameters.description: Reverts the mesh toward its original state, or smooths an already-warped mesh.

parameters.name: Twirl Clockwise (C)
parameters.description: Rotates pixels under the brush; hold Alt/Opt to twirl counter-clockwise.

parameters.name: Pucker (S) / Bloat (B)
parameters.description: Contracts pixels toward, or expands them away from, the brush centre.

parameters.name: Push Left (O)
parameters.description: Displaces pixels perpendicular to the drag direction - good for straightening edges.

parameters.name: Freeze Mask (F) / Thaw Mask (D)
parameters.description: Paints a protective mask so brushed areas are not deformed, and removes it again.

parameters.name: Face tool (A)
parameters.description: On-canvas handles for Face-Aware Liquify; the right-hand panel adds Eyes, Nose, Mouth and Face Shape sliders plus a Select Face menu for multiple faces.

parameters.name: Brush Tool Options
parameters.description: Size, Density (edge feathering), Pressure (strength), Rate (speed for held tools), and Pin Edges to lock the image border.

parameters.name: Load Mesh / Save Mesh
parameters.description: Stores the deformation mesh to a .msh file so the same warp can be reapplied to another image.

parameters.name: View Options
parameters.description: Show Guides, Show Face Overlay, Show Image, Show Mesh (with mesh size/color) and Show Backdrop to reference other layers.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Convert for Smart Filters so the warp stays re-editable.
2. Choose Filter > Liquify... (Shift+Ctrl+X).
3. Use Freeze Mask (F) to protect the background near the subject's edge.
4. Pick Forward Warp (W), set Size ~250, Density 50, Pressure 30, and make short gentle strokes.
5. For a portrait, switch to the Face tool (A) and use the Eyes and Face Shape sliders instead of freehand warping.
6. Save Mesh if you need to repeat the same warp on a bracketed frame, then click OK.
tools.notes: Works as a Smart Filter, which is the only practical way to revise a warp later. Face-Aware sliders are greyed out when no face is detected - crop tighter or increase resolution. Large brushes on very large documents are memory-hungry; enable the GPU in Preferences > Performance for smooth previews. There is no ExtendScript DOM method for Liquify; automate it with an Action or a saved mesh.

tools.name: Vanishing Point
tools.description: Lets you define perspective planes on an image (the face of a building, a road, a box) and then clone, heal, paint, paste and transform content so that it automatically follows that perspective - scaling and skewing as it moves into the distance. Planes can be torn off at 90 degrees or arbitrary angles to wrap around corners, and the resulting grids can be rendered to a layer or exported for After Effects and 3D applications. Use it for removing objects from perspective surfaces, extending walls and floors, and pasting artwork onto angled signage or packaging.

parameters.name: Create Plane tool (C)
parameters.description: Click four corner points to define a perspective plane; the grid turns blue when valid, yellow or red when the perspective is implausible.

parameters.name: Edit Plane tool (V)
parameters.description: Selects, moves and resizes an existing plane; Ctrl/Cmd-drag an edge handle to tear off a perpendicular plane.

parameters.name: Marquee tool (M)
parameters.description: Perspective-aware selection with Feather, Opacity, Heal (Off/Luminance/On) and Move Mode (Destination/Source).

parameters.name: Stamp tool (S)
parameters.description: Perspective clone stamp; Alt/Opt-click to set the source, and use Heal to blend tone and texture.

parameters.name: Brush tool (B)
parameters.description: Paints with a chosen color in perspective, with Diameter, Hardness, Opacity and Heal options.

parameters.name: Transform tool (T)
parameters.description: Moves, scales and flips a floating selection or pasted content inside the plane.

parameters.name: Eyedropper (I) / Measure (K)
parameters.description: Samples a paint color from the image, and measures distances and angles on a plane.

parameters.name: Grid Size / Angle
parameters.description: Controls the spacing of the grid and the angle of a tear-off plane.

parameters.name: Fly-out menu
parameters.description: Render Grids to Photoshop, Export for After Effects (.vpe), and Return 3D Layer to Photoshop options.

tools.example:
1. Add a new empty layer above the image (Ctrl+Shift+N) and keep it selected so the result lands on its own layer.
2. Choose Filter > Vanishing Point... (Alt+Ctrl+V).
3. With the Create Plane tool, click the four corners of the wall; adjust until the grid is blue.
4. Ctrl-drag a side handle to tear off a second plane around the corner.
5. Pick the Stamp tool, set Heal to On, Alt-click a clean area, and paint out the object.
6. To paste artwork, copy it in Photoshop first, then press Ctrl+V inside Vanishing Point and drag it onto the plane.
7. Click OK.
tools.notes: Vanishing Point cannot be applied as a Smart Filter, so always work on a new empty layer to stay non-destructive. Content copied for pasting must be on the clipboard before you open the dialog. Planes are saved with the PSD, so reopening the filter restores them. It works on 8- and 16-bit RGB/Grayscale/CMYK/Lab documents.

tools.name: Neural Filters
tools.description: A separate workspace hosting Adobe's machine-learning filters, each downloaded on demand and run either on your GPU/CPU or partly in the cloud. The gallery is split into Featured filters (production-ready) and Beta filters (still evolving), and several filters can be chained in one session before you commit. Its Output menu is the key control: it decides whether the result overwrites the layer, lands on a new layer, becomes a Smart Filter or opens as a new document.

parameters.name: Skin Smoothing
parameters.description: Featured. One-click blemish and texture smoothing for portraits (Blur, Smoothness).

parameters.name: Smart Portrait
parameters.description: Featured. Generative portrait edits: Happiness, Surprise, Anger, Facial Age, Gaze, Hair Thickness, Head Direction, Light Direction.

parameters.name: Super Zoom
parameters.description: Featured. Upscales a crop and synthesises the detail lost to the enlargement.

parameters.name: JPEG Artifacts Removal
parameters.description: Featured. Removes blocking and ringing artifacts left by heavy JPEG compression.

parameters.name: Colorize
parameters.description: Featured. Adds plausible color to black-and-white photographs, with optional focal points.

parameters.name: Style Transfer
parameters.description: Featured. Applies the painterly style of a preset or custom reference image to your photo.

parameters.name: Makeup Transfer
parameters.description: Featured. Copies eye and mouth makeup from one open image to another.

parameters.name: Photo Restoration
parameters.description: Beta. Repairs scratches, dust and fading in scanned prints, with a dedicated face enhancement pass.

parameters.name: Harmonization
parameters.description: Beta. Matches the color and tone of one layer to a reference layer for compositing.

parameters.name: Landscape Mixer
parameters.description: Beta. Blends a landscape with a reference image and shifts season and time of day.

parameters.name: Depth Blur
parameters.description: Beta. Estimates scene depth and blurs foreground or background, with haze and color-temperature controls.

parameters.name: Color Transfer
parameters.description: Beta. Transfers the color palette of a reference image onto your image.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Current Layer, New Layer, New Layer Masked, Smart Filter, or New Document - choose Smart Filter or New Layer to stay non-destructive.

tools.example:
1. Open an image and select the pixel layer.
2. Choose Filter > Neural Filters...
3. Click the Download (cloud) icon next to the filter you want; wait for the model to install.
4. Toggle the filter switch on and adjust its sliders in the right-hand panel.
5. Set Output to Smart Filter (or New Layer) at the bottom left.
6. Click OK.
tools.notes: Requires macOS 10.15+ or Windows 10+ and an 8-bit RGB document; convert 16/32-bit images with Image > Mode > 8 Bits/Channel first. Each filter is a separate download ranging from under 1 MB (Skin Smoothing) to over 650 MB (Style Transfer). Filters that process in the cloud (for example Smart Portrait and Depth Blur) need an internet connection and an Adobe sign-in. Beta filters can change or be withdrawn between releases, so do not build an unattended pipeline on them. There is no ExtendScript DOM API for Neural Filters.

tools.name: Skin Smoothing (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Detects faces and smooths blemishes, spots, acne and uneven skin texture in a single pass while leaving eyes, lips, hair and the image background untouched. It is far quicker than a frequency-separation retouch and good enough for web-sized portraits, headshots and event photography. Use a light setting as a base pass and finish the remaining detail by hand.
tools.usage: Filter > Neural Filters... > Featured > Skin Smoothing

parameters.name: Blur
parameters.description: How strongly the skin texture is softened. High values quickly look plastic.

parameters.name: Smoothness
parameters.description: How aggressively blemishes and tonal unevenness are evened out.

parameters.name: Select Face
parameters.description: Dropdown for picking which detected face the sliders affect when several are present.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Current Layer, New Layer, New Layer Masked, Smart Filter or New Document.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Neural Filters... and download Skin Smoothing if prompted (it is the smallest model, under 1 MB).
2. Toggle Skin Smoothing on; Photoshop highlights the detected face.
3. Set Blur around 25 and Smoothness around 40 for a natural result.
4. Set Output to New Layer Masked and click OK.
5. Lower the new layer's opacity, or paint black on its mask, to bring texture back where it is missing.
tools.notes: Requires an 8-bit RGB document and a detectable face - profile shots, heavy occlusion, or very small faces may not register. Works on one face at a time; for group shots re-run the filter per face using Select Face. Output to New Layer Masked makes the result easy to dial back.

tools.name: Super Zoom (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Enlarges a crop of an image and uses a trained model to invent the detail that the enlargement would otherwise lose, so the result stays sharper than bicubic or Preserve Details resampling. It can also clean up noise and JPEG artifacts and sharpen facial features as part of the same pass. Use it to rescue a tight crop, to enlarge a small web image for print, or to recover usable resolution from an old file.
tools.usage: Filter > Neural Filters... > Featured > Super Zoom

parameters.name: Zoom (+ / -)
parameters.description: Magnification steps (2x, 4x, and so on); pan the preview to choose the region to enlarge.

parameters.name: Enhance Image Detail
parameters.description: Adds synthesised micro-detail to the upscaled result.

parameters.name: Enhance Face Details
parameters.description: Runs an extra face-specific pass to sharpen eyes, lashes and lips.

parameters.name: Reduce Noise
parameters.description: Suppresses sensor noise amplified by the upscale.

parameters.name: Reduce JPEG Artifacts
parameters.description: Removes blocking and ringing from compressed sources.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Super Zoom always produces a larger canvas, so New Document is usually the right output choice.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Super Zoom and download the model if needed.
2. Pan the preview to the area you want to keep and click + to set the zoom factor.
3. Enable Enhance Image Detail, and Enhance Face Details if the crop contains a face.
4. Add a little Reduce Noise / Reduce JPEG Artifacts if the source is compressed.
5. Set Output to New Document and click OK.
tools.notes: 8-bit RGB only. The model invents detail rather than recovering it, so the output is not evidentiary - never use it for forensic or scientific work. For a purely mathematical enlargement use Image > Image Size with Resample: Preserve Details 2.0 instead.

tools.name: Colorize (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Analyses a black-and-white photograph and predicts plausible colors for skin, sky, foliage, clothing and architecture, turning a monochrome scan into a color image in one step. Focal points let you override the prediction locally by dropping a marker and choosing the exact color you want in that region. Use it on family archive scans, historical prints and any greyscale artwork that needs a colour starting point.

parameters.name: Profile
parameters.description: Preset colorization profiles that bias the model toward different palettes.

parameters.name: Focal points
parameters.description: Click Add colour to focal point, click a spot in the image, then pick a colour to force that region toward it.

parameters.name: Color artifact reduction
parameters.description: Suppresses colour bleeding and blotching at high-contrast edges.

parameters.name: Saturation
parameters.description: Overall strength of the predicted colour.

parameters.name: Cyan / Red, Magenta / Green, Yellow / Blue
parameters.description: Three global colour-balance sliders for correcting an overall cast.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: New Layer or Smart Filter keeps the original greyscale intact underneath.

tools.example:
1. Convert the scan with Image > Mode > RGB Color and Image > Mode > 8 Bits/Channel.
2. Choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Colorize and toggle it on.
3. If a jacket comes out the wrong colour, click Add colour to focal point, click the jacket and pick the correct hue.
4. Trim Saturation back and raise Color artifact reduction if edges bleed.
5. Set Output to New Layer and click OK, then mask or repaint any stubborn regions by hand.
tools.notes: Requires an 8-bit RGB document - a Grayscale file must be converted to RGB first or the filter stays greyed out. Faded or badly exposed originals give poor colour predictions; run a Curves or Camera Raw contrast correction before colorizing. Results are an interpretation, not a restoration of the original colours.

tools.name: Style Transfer (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Applies the visual style of a reference artwork - brushwork, palette, texture - to the content of your photograph, using a set of built-in presets or any image you supply. Controls let you decide how strongly the style is imposed, whether the photograph's original colours survive, and whether the subject stays sharp while the background takes the full effect. Use it for stylised posters, concept art backplates and quick painterly treatments.
tools.usage: Filter > Neural Filters... > Featured > Style Transfer

parameters.name: Artist / Style presets
parameters.description: Thumbnail grid of bundled styles; the Custom tab lets you load your own reference image.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: How far the image is pushed toward the reference style.

parameters.name: Style Opacity
parameters.description: Blends the stylised result back over the untouched original.

parameters.name: Brush Size
parameters.description: Scale of the synthesised brush texture.

parameters.name: Preserve Color
parameters.description: Keeps the original photograph's colours while adopting only the reference's texture and stroke.

parameters.name: Focus Subject
parameters.description: Detects the subject and reduces the stylisation over it.

parameters.name: Blur Background
parameters.description: Softens the stylised background to push the subject forward.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Smart Filter or New Layer, so the stylisation can be masked and faded afterwards.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Style Transfer (this is the largest download, over 600 MB).
2. Pick a preset thumbnail, or open Custom and load your own reference painting.
3. Set Strength around 50, then enable Preserve Color if the photo's own palette matters.
4. Turn on Focus Subject so the face stays readable.
5. Set Output to New Layer and click OK; mask the layer to restore detail where you need it.
tools.notes: 8-bit RGB only. Very large documents are downsampled internally, so the returned texture scale may not match a print-resolution file - run it on a smaller copy and upscale, or accept the softer detail. The bundled presets are styles, not licensed reproductions of specific artworks.

tools.name: Depth Blur (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Estimates a depth map for the scene from a single photograph and uses it to blur the background or foreground, simulating a shallow depth of field without any hand-painted mask. It can also add atmospheric haze at distance and shift the temperature, brightness and saturation of the far part of the scene. Use it on phone snaps and deep-focus images to create separation between subject and background.
tools.usage: Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Depth Blur

parameters.name: Subject Focus
parameters.description: Click a point in the preview to set what stays sharp.

parameters.name: Focal Distance
parameters.description: Moves the plane of sharp focus forward or back through the estimated depth.

parameters.name: Blur Strength
parameters.description: How much defocus is applied away from the focal plane.

parameters.name: Focus Subject
parameters.description: Automatically keeps the detected subject sharp instead of relying on a clicked point.

parameters.name: Haze
parameters.description: Adds atmospheric haze that increases with distance.

parameters.name: Warmth / Brightness / Saturation
parameters.description: Colour and tone shifts applied to the blurred, distant part of the scene.

parameters.name: Grain
parameters.description: Re-adds grain so the blurred region matches the sharp region's noise.

parameters.name: Output Depth Map Only
parameters.description: Returns the estimated greyscale depth map instead of a blurred image - useful as a source for Filter > Blur > Lens Blur or for masking.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Depth Blur and toggle it on.
2. Click the subject in the preview to set Subject Focus, or enable Focus Subject.
3. Raise Blur Strength until the background separates, then add a little Haze for depth.
4. Add Grain to match the sharp areas.
5. For maximum control, instead tick Output Depth Map Only, set Output to New Layer, then load that map as an alpha channel and drive Filter > Blur > Lens Blur with it.
6. Set Output to Smart Filter and click OK.
tools.notes: A Beta filter; part of the processing runs in the cloud, so an internet connection and Adobe sign-in are required. 8-bit RGB only. Depth estimation fails on flat subjects, reflections and glass, producing halos at the subject edge - inspect the edge at 100% and mask by hand where needed. When chained with other Neural Filters the progress dialog may not appear until processing finishes.

tools.name: Photo Restoration (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Repairs damaged scans of old prints: it reduces scratches, dust, creases and halftone patterning, recovers contrast and micro-detail, and runs a separate pass to reconstruct facial features. It is the fastest first step for an archive-scanning project, leaving only the worst tears for manual healing. Combine it with Colorize to turn a damaged monochrome print into a clean colour image.
tools.usage: Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Photo Restoration

parameters.name: Photo Enhancement
parameters.description: Overall restoration strength - contrast, detail recovery and general clean-up.

parameters.name: Enhance Face
parameters.description: Extra reconstruction pass for detected faces (eyes, mouth, hair).

parameters.name: Scratch Reduction
parameters.description: Targets scratches, dust specks and creases.

parameters.name: Adjustment > Photo noise reduction
parameters.description: Smooths grain and sensor/scanner noise.

parameters.name: Adjustment > Colour noise reduction
parameters.description: Removes chroma blotching from faded or stained prints.

parameters.name: Adjustment > Halftone artifacts removal
parameters.description: Suppresses the printing screen pattern picked up when scanning a printed photograph.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: New Layer or Smart Filter so the original scan stays untouched.

tools.example:
1. Scan the print at 600 ppi or higher and open it in Photoshop.
2. Choose Image > Mode > 8 Bits/Channel and RGB Color if needed.
3. Choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Photo Restoration.
4. Set Photo Enhancement around 50, Enhance Face around 50 and Scratch Reduction to taste.
5. Enable Halftone artifacts removal if you scanned a printed reproduction.
6. Set Output to New Layer, click OK, then heal remaining tears with the Spot Healing Brush.
tools.notes: Beta filter, 8-bit RGB only, and the model is a separate download. Enhance Face can subtly change identity on very low-resolution faces - compare against the original before delivering restoration work. Large tears and missing corners still need Content-Aware Fill or the Clone Stamp.

tools.name: Harmonization (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Matches the colour and tone of the active layer to a chosen reference layer so a pasted element sits convincingly in its new scene. Rather than a global Match Color, it analyses the lighting of the reference and remaps the subject's colour, contrast and brightness to suit it. Use it as the first pass of any composite, then refine with adjustment layers clipped to the subject.

parameters.name: Reference layer
parameters.description: Dropdown listing the other layers in the document; pick the background you want the subject to match.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: How far the active layer is pushed toward the reference's colour and tone.

parameters.name: Advanced refinement sliders
parameters.description: Secondary controls for tweaking the brightness, saturation and colour balance of the harmonised result.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: New Layer or Smart Filter keeps the un-harmonised cut-out available.

tools.example:
1. Place the cut-out subject on its own layer above the background layer.
2. With the subject layer active, choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Harmonization.
3. Choose the background in the Reference layer dropdown.
4. Set Strength to around 75 and refine with the secondary sliders.
5. Set Output to New Layer and click OK, then add a clipped Curves layer for final matching.
tools.notes: Beta filter; needs at least two layers in the document and an 8-bit RGB file. The subject layer should already be cleanly masked - Harmonization matches colour, it does not fix a bad cut-out. It cannot match direction of light or add cast shadows, which still have to be painted.

tools.name: Landscape Mixer (Neural Filter)
tools.description: Blends your landscape photograph with a reference landscape - either a bundled preset or an image you supply - pulling elements, palette and atmosphere from both to produce a new scene. Season and time-of-day sliders let you turn a summer shot into an autumn or winter one, or a midday scene into a sunset, without masking anything. Use it for concept art, mood exploration and quick season variants of a stock landscape.
tools.usage: Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Landscape Mixer

parameters.name: Preset / Custom reference
parameters.description: Choose one of the bundled reference landscapes, or load your own image on the Custom tab.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: How much of the reference landscape's character is mixed into your image.

parameters.name: Winter / Spring / Summer / Fall
parameters.description: Season sliders that shift foliage colour, snow cover and overall palette.

parameters.name: Sunset
parameters.description: Shifts the scene toward golden-hour or sunset lighting.

parameters.name: Preserve Subject
parameters.description: Protects a detected foreground subject from being repainted by the mix.

parameters.name: Harmonize Subject
parameters.description: Colour-matches the protected subject to the new landscape so it does not look pasted in.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: New Layer or Smart Filter so the original landscape survives underneath.

tools.example:
1. Open a wide landscape shot and choose Filter > Neural Filters... > Beta > Landscape Mixer.
2. Click a preset reference thumbnail, or load your own sunset shot under Custom.
3. Set Strength to around 50, then raise Fall to turn summer foliage golden.
4. Enable Preserve Subject and Harmonize Subject if a person or building is in the foreground.
5. Set Output to New Layer and click OK; mask back any areas the model repainted badly.
tools.notes: Beta filter, 8-bit RGB only. It hallucinates terrain and sky content, so straight lines, buildings and recognisable landmarks can be distorted - never present the output as a documentary photograph. Works best on open scenes with a clear horizon; it struggles with dense forest and close-up detail.

tools.name: Gaussian Blur
tools.description: Softens the image by convolving it with a bell-shaped (Gaussian) weighting curve, controlled by a single Radius value. It is the general-purpose blur of Photoshop: used for smoothing masks and selections, building glows and drop shadows, faking depth of field, and as the low-frequency half of a frequency-separation retouch. Larger radii add a hazy, low-frequency wash; very small radii just take the edge off aliasing.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Blur width in pixels. The ExtendScript method accepts 1.0 to 250.0; the dialog itself accepts fractional values down to 0.1.

parameters.name: Preview
parameters.description: Live canvas preview; click and hold inside the dialog's thumbnail to compare with the original.

tools.notes: When applied inside a selection, Gaussian Blur pulls in colour from outside the selection edge, which contaminates the result with a fringe - use Smart Blur, Surface Blur or Lens Blur when that matters. Blur the layer mask rather than the pixels if you only want a softer transition. Convert to a Smart Object first to keep the Radius editable. Supports 8-, 16- and 32-bit documents.

tools.name: Motion Blur
tools.description: Smears pixels along a single straight direction, imitating a photograph of a moving subject taken with a long exposure. You set the angle of travel and the distance the smear covers. Use it to add speed to a cut-out subject, to soften a background into a sense of panning, and as the basis for light-streak and brushed-metal textures.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Direction of the smear in degrees; the ExtendScript method accepts -360 to 360. Drag the dial in the dialog to set it visually.

parameters.name: Distance
parameters.description: Length of the streak in pixels; the ExtendScript method accepts 1 to 999.

tools.notes: Like Gaussian Blur, it samples pixels from outside a selection edge and therefore contaminates the boundary - blur on a duplicate layer and mask instead. The filter blurs symmetrically in both directions along the angle, so a subject appears to smear forward and backward; mask off the leading edge to fake directional motion. For rotational or zoom movement use Radial Blur, and for a path-driven or strobed smear use Blur Gallery > Path Blur or Spin Blur.

tools.name: Radial Blur
tools.description: Simulates the blur of a rotating or zooming camera. Spin mode blurs along concentric circles around a centre point; Zoom mode blurs along radial lines as if the lens were zoomed during the exposure. Use it for spinning wheels and propellers, for explosive zoom-burst backgrounds, and for radiating light effects.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: Strength of the blur, 1 to 100 - degrees of rotation in Spin mode, or the zoom extent in Zoom mode.

parameters.name: Blur Method
parameters.description: Spin (concentric rotation) or Zoom (radial streaks from the centre).

parameters.name: Quality
parameters.description: Draft (fast, grainy), Good, or Best (smoothest, slowest).

parameters.name: Blur Center
parameters.description: Drag the pattern inside the Blur Center box to move the origin of the effect.

tools.notes: The dialog gives no live canvas preview - only the small Blur Center grid - so work on a duplicate layer and undo/redo to judge the result. Best quality is markedly slower on large documents; prototype at Draft. Blur Gallery > Spin Blur is the modern, on-canvas alternative for rotational blur with an elliptical shape and strobe control.

tools.name: Lens Blur
tools.description: Simulates an optical defocus rather than a mathematical blur: it reproduces the iris shape of a real lens, blooms specular highlights into bokeh discs, and can vary the amount of blur across the frame from a depth map stored in an alpha channel or layer mask. This is the right filter for convincing shallow depth of field because the highlights behave the way a real out-of-focus lens renders them. Use it after building a depth map by hand, from a gradient, or from the Depth Blur Neural Filter's Output Depth Map Only option.

parameters.name: Depth Map > Source
parameters.description: None, Transparency, Layer Mask, or any alpha channel - white areas blur most unless Invert is on.

parameters.name: Blur Focal Distance
parameters.description: Which grey level in the depth map stays sharp (0-255); you can also click the preview to set it.

parameters.name: Invert
parameters.description: Reverses the depth map so black rather than white is the blurred end.

parameters.name: Iris > Shape
parameters.description: Iris geometry: Triangle, Square, Pentagon, Hexagon, Heptagon or Octagon - controls the shape of the bokeh discs.

parameters.name: Iris > Radius
parameters.description: Overall blur amount, 0 to 100.

parameters.name: Iris > Blade Curvature / Rotation
parameters.description: Rounds and rotates the iris blades, changing the bokeh outline.

parameters.name: Specular Highlights > Brightness / Threshold
parameters.description: How brightly highlights bloom, and which luminance level counts as a highlight.

parameters.name: Noise > Amount / Distribution / Monochromatic
parameters.description: Re-adds grain to the blurred region so it matches the un-blurred parts.

parameters.name: Preview
parameters.description: Faster or More Accurate - Lens Blur is expensive, so preview on Faster while setting up.

tools.example:
// Lens Blur using the layer transparency as the depth map
var doc = app.activeDocument;
doc.activeLayer.applyLensBlur(
  DepthMapSource.NONE,   // source
  0,                     // focalDistance
  false,                 // invertDepthMap
  Geometry.HEXAGON,      // iris shape
  15,                    // radius
  0,                     // bladeCurvature
  0,                     // rotation
  50,                    // specular highlight brightness
  200,                   // specular highlight threshold
  2,                     // noise amount
  NoiseDistribution.UNIFORM,
  true                   // monochromatic noise
);
tools.notes: Lens Blur is not GPU accelerated and is slow on large files; set Preview to Faster while adjusting. It does not honour a selection the way other blurs do - use the depth map or a Smart Filter mask. Photoshop 25 and later also ships a separate, AI-driven Lens Blur panel inside Camera Raw / Filter > Camera Raw Filter that generates its own depth map automatically; that one is generally easier for photographs, while this filter gives explicit iris and highlight control.

tools.name: Smart Blur
tools.description: Blurs areas of similar tone while leaving edges intact, by only averaging pixels whose difference falls below a threshold. Because it does not pull colour across a selection boundary it avoids the muddy fringe that Gaussian Blur produces, and it is a quick way to flatten skin, sky or noise without losing outlines. Its Edge Only and Overlay Edge modes turn it into an edge-detector that is useful for comic and poster effects.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Size of the neighbourhood searched for dissimilar pixels; the ExtendScript method accepts 0 to 1000.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: How different two pixels must be before the filter treats the difference as an edge and stops blurring; 0 to 1000 in script.

parameters.name: Quality
parameters.description: Low, Medium or High - controls the smoothness of the result.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Normal (blur the image), Edge Only (white edges on black), or Overlay Edge (the blurred image with white edges drawn over it).

tools.notes: 8-bit only in practice - Smart Blur is greyed out on 16- and 32-bit documents, so convert down (or use Surface Blur, which supports 16-bit). High radius with a high threshold produces a posterised, plastic look; keep the threshold low for subtle work. Edge Only mode replaces the image entirely, so run it on a duplicate layer.

tools.name: Surface Blur
tools.description: Blurs flat surfaces while preserving edges, using a radius for the sample area and a threshold that excludes neighbouring pixels whose tonal difference is too large. It is the go-to filter for reducing skin texture, sensor noise and scan grain without softening the outlines of features. Compared with Smart Blur it gives a smoother, more photographic result and works on 16-bit files.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Size of the area sampled for the blur in pixels - larger values smooth broader areas.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: How far a neighbouring pixel's tonal value may diverge from the centre pixel before it is excluded from the blur; keeps edges sharp.

tools.example:
1. Duplicate the retouch layer (Ctrl+J) so the effect is reversible.
2. Choose Filter > Blur > Surface Blur...
3. Start with Radius about 12 and Threshold about 12, then raise Radius until the texture disappears.
4. Lower Threshold until the edges of eyes, lips and hair come back crisp.
5. Click OK, add a black layer mask, and paint white only over the areas that should be smoothed.
tools.notes: Supports 8- and 16-bit documents but not 32-bit. It is slow on large radii because of the per-pixel threshold test. There is no ExtendScript DOM method for Surface Blur - record an Action or build an executeAction descriptor to script it.

tools.name: Box Blur & Average
tools.description: Two simple averaging blurs at opposite ends of the scale. Box Blur replaces each pixel with the unweighted average of a square neighbourhood, which gives a harder, more mechanical softening than Gaussian and is prized for chunky glow and glass effects. Average collapses the whole image or selection to a single flat colour - the mean of everything inside it - which is the fastest way to read a scene's average colour for white-balance or colour-grading work.
tools.usage: Filter > Blur > Box Blur... and Filter > Blur > Average

parameters.name: Box Blur > Radius
parameters.description: Half-width of the square averaging kernel in pixels; larger radii blur more and the squareness of the kernel becomes visible at high values.

parameters.name: Average
parameters.description: No dialog and no options - it fills the image or the active selection with the average colour immediately.

tools.example:
1. Box Blur: select the layer, choose Filter > Blur > Box Blur..., set Radius to 20 and click OK.
2. Average for colour matching: make a selection over a neutral area, duplicate the layer (Ctrl+J), choose Filter > Blur > Average.
3. Sample the resulting flat colour with the Eyedropper to read the scene's average.
4. Or invert that average colour and blend it back at low opacity as a quick white-balance correction.
tools.notes: Both support 8-, 16- and 32-bit documents. Box Blur is another filter that pulls colour in from outside a selection edge, so expect a fringe if you blur a selected region in place. Average applied without a selection flattens the whole layer to one colour - always work on a duplicate. Neither has a dedicated ExtendScript DOM method.

tools.name: Blur Gallery
tools.description: A single on-canvas workspace hosting five pin-driven blurs - Field Blur, Iris Blur, Tilt-Shift, Path Blur and Spin Blur - which can be combined in one session and share the Effects, Motion Effects and Noise panels. Instead of a dialog you drop pins directly on the image and drag rings and handles to shape where and how much blur falls, with a full-size live preview. Use it for selective focus, miniature-faking, panning and rotation effects, and for adding realistic bokeh to any of them.
tools.usage: Filter > Blur Gallery > Field Blur / Iris Blur / Tilt-Shift / Path Blur / Spin Blur

parameters.name: Field Blur
parameters.description: Drop multiple pins, each with its own blur value, to build a gradient of focus across the whole frame - the most flexible of the five.

parameters.name: Iris Blur
parameters.description: An elliptical (or rounded-rectangular) sharp zone with an adjustable feather ring; everything outside it blurs. Classic selective-focus vignette.

parameters.name: Tilt-Shift
parameters.description: A band of sharpness between two lines that fades to blur above and below, simulating a tilt-shift lens; adds Distortion and Symmetric Distortion controls for the miniature-model look.

parameters.name: Path Blur
parameters.description: Blurs along one or more editable paths you draw on the image, with Speed, Taper, End Point Speed and Centered Blur / Rear Sync Flash - for directional motion that follows a curve.

parameters.name: Spin Blur
parameters.description: Rotational blur inside an adjustable ellipse with a movable rotation centre and Blur Angle - for wheels, turntables and propellers.

parameters.name: Effects panel
parameters.description: Bokeh controls for Field, Iris and Tilt-Shift: Light Bokeh (brightens out-of-focus areas), Bokeh Color (saturates the lightened areas) and Light Range (which tones are affected).

parameters.name: Motion Effects panel
parameters.description: Strobe Strength, Strobe Flashes and Strobe Flash Duration for Path Blur and Spin Blur, emulating multiple flash pops during the exposure.

parameters.name: Noise panel
parameters.description: Re-adds Gaussian, Uniform or Grain noise to the blurred region (Amount, Size, Roughness, Color, Highlights) so it matches the sharp areas.

parameters.name: Options bar
parameters.description: Save Mask to Channels, High Quality preview, Focus percentage, Preview toggle and Remove All Pins.

tools.example:
1. Choose Filter > Convert for Smart Filters so the pins stay editable.
2. Choose Filter > Blur Gallery > Iris Blur.
3. Drag the outer ellipse to cover the subject, drag the four white feather dots inward to tighten the falloff, and drag the pin's ring to set the blur amount.
4. Click elsewhere on the image to add a second pin if you need a second zone of focus.
5. Open the Effects panel and raise Light Bokeh to about 20% for highlight bloom.
6. Open the Noise panel and add a little Grain so the blur matches the rest of the frame.
7. Press M to inspect the blur mask, then click OK in the options bar.
tools.notes: All five sub-blurs live in one modal session - you can stack, for example, a Tilt-Shift and a Field Blur pin set before committing. Applying them as a Smart Filter is the only way to re-open the pins later. Tick Save Mask to Channels to get the blur mask as an alpha channel. The gallery is GPU accelerated; if it is greyed out or slow, enable Use Graphics Processor in Preferences > Performance. There is no ExtendScript DOM method - script it via an Action or an executeAction descriptor.

tools.name: Displace
tools.description: Distorts the layer by reading a second image, the displacement map, and shifting each pixel horizontally and vertically according to the brightness values it finds there. Because the map can be any greyscale or RGB PSD, this is the standard technique for wrapping artwork realistically onto fabric, skin, crumpled paper or water. Use it when a simple Warp transform looks too flat and you need the surface texture to modulate the distortion.

parameters.name: Horizontal Scale
parameters.description: Strength of the sideways shift, -999 to 999 - how far a mid-grey deviation moves a pixel.

parameters.name: Vertical Scale
parameters.description: Strength of the up/down shift, -999 to 999.

parameters.name: Displacement Map
parameters.description: Stretch To Fit (resize the map to the layer) or Tile (repeat it).

parameters.name: Undefined Areas
parameters.description: Wrap Around (bring in pixels from the opposite edge) or Repeat Edge Pixels (smear the border).

parameters.name: Map file
parameters.description: After clicking OK the filter asks for a flattened .psd file to use as the map; a single-layer greyscale PSD works best.

tools.notes: The displacement map must be a flattened .psd - other formats are rejected. Build the map by duplicating the target surface, desaturating it, applying a small Gaussian Blur and saving it as a separate PSD. Mid-grey (128) means no displacement, black shifts one way and white the other. Combine the displaced artwork with a Multiply or Soft Light blend mode so the underlying texture shows through.

tools.name: Pinch
tools.description: Squeezes or expands the image toward or away from the centre of the selection, as if it were printed on a rubber sheet being pushed in or pulled out. Positive amounts pull pixels inward, negative amounts push them outward into a bulge. Use it for subtle facial slimming inside an elliptical selection, for caricature effects, and for bending flat artwork onto a concave or convex surface.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: -100% to 100%. Positive values shift pixels toward the centre (pinch), negative values push them outward (bulge).

parameters.name: Preview grid
parameters.description: The dialog shows a wireframe mesh illustrating how the grid is deformed.

tools.example:
// Gentle inward pinch on the active layer
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.applyPinch(25);   // amount, -100 to 100
tools.notes: The effect is centred on the active selection's bounding box, so make a circular or elliptical selection with a generous feather before applying - an unfeathered selection leaves a visible seam. Does not work on images larger than 11500 x 11500 pixels. For a spherical rather than conical falloff use Spherize; for freehand control use Liquify's Pucker and Bloat tools.

tools.name: Polar Coordinates
tools.description: Remaps the image between rectangular and polar coordinate systems. Rectangular To Polar wraps the image into a circle, turning a panorama into a 'tiny planet'; Polar To Rectangular unrolls a circular image into a flat strip. It also reproduces cylinder anamorphosis, the 18th-century art form in which a deliberately distorted image reads correctly when viewed in a mirrored cylinder.

parameters.name: Rectangular To Polar
parameters.description: Wraps the image into a disc - the bottom edge becomes the centre and the top edge becomes the outer rim.

parameters.name: Polar To Rectangular
parameters.description: Unrolls a circular or fisheye image into a flat rectangular strip.

tools.notes: For a convincing tiny planet, first make the canvas square (Image > Image Size with Constrain Proportions off) and flip the image vertically (Image > Image Rotation > Flip Canvas Vertical) so the sky ends up on the outside. A seam always appears where the left and right edges meet - heal it afterwards with the Spot Healing Brush or by offsetting and blending the panorama first with Filter > Other > Offset.

tools.name: Ripple, Wave & ZigZag
tools.description: Three related Distort filters that push pixels along periodic waveforms. Ripple is the simple one - an undulating pattern with just an amount and a size. Wave exposes the full generator model (number of generators, wavelength, amplitude, scale and waveform shape) for precise or chaotic distortions. ZigZag distorts radially from the centre of the selection and is the standard way to fake water ripples on a pond. Use them for water and heat-haze effects, for animated-looking type, and for flag and fabric distortion.
tools.usage: Filter > Distort > Ripple... , Filter > Distort > Wave... , Filter > Distort > ZigZag...

parameters.name: Ripple > Amount
parameters.description: Strength of the undulation, -999 to 999.

parameters.name: Ripple > Size
parameters.description: Small, Medium or Large wavelength.

parameters.name: Wave > Number of Generators
parameters.description: How many superimposed waves are combined, 1 to 999 - more generators give a more chaotic result.

parameters.name: Wave > Wavelength (Min/Max)
parameters.description: Crest-to-crest distance range; Min 1 to 998, Max from Min+1 upward.

parameters.name: Wave > Amplitude (Min/Max)
parameters.description: Height of the wave range; Min 1 to 998, Max from Min+1 upward.

parameters.name: Wave > Scale (Horiz/Vert)
parameters.description: Percentage of the distortion applied on each axis, 1 to 100.

parameters.name: Wave > Type
parameters.description: Sine (smooth rolling), Triangle (angular) or Square (hard-edged banding).

parameters.name: Wave > Undefined Areas / Randomize
parameters.description: Wrap Around or Repeat Edge Pixels for the emptied border, and a Randomize button that reseeds the generators.

parameters.name: ZigZag > Amount
parameters.description: Strength of the radial distortion, -100 to 100.

parameters.name: ZigZag > Ridges
parameters.description: Number of direction reversals between the centre of the selection and its edge.

parameters.name: ZigZag > Style
parameters.description: Pond Ripples (displaces up-left and down-right), Out From Center, or Around Center (rotates pixels around the centre).

tools.notes: All three are centred on, or clipped by, the active selection - feather the selection generously or the distortion stops abruptly at its edge. ZigZag does not work on images larger than 8000 x 8000 pixels. Wave's Max wavelength and amplitude must exceed the corresponding Min or the dialog refuses the value. Apply to a Smart Object to keep the settings editable, since these distortions are hard to dial in first time.

tools.name: Shear
tools.description: Bends the image along a curve that you draw by dragging control points on a vertical line in the dialog. The distortion is applied vertically, so to shear horizontally you rotate the layer 90 degrees, apply the filter and rotate back. Use it for bending text and artwork onto a curved surface, for flag-like waves, and for correcting a gently bowed scan.

parameters.name: Curve
parameters.description: Click the vertical line in the dialog to add control points and drag them sideways; in ExtendScript the curve is passed as an array of [x, y] point pairs.

parameters.name: Undefined Areas
parameters.description: Wrap Around (bring in pixels from the opposite edge) or Repeat Edge Pixels (smear the border outward).

parameters.name: Default
parameters.description: Button that resets the curve to a straight vertical line.

tools.notes: Shear only distorts vertically. For a horizontal bend, use Image > Image Rotation > 90 degrees Counter Clockwise, apply Shear, then rotate back. The distortion is confined to the layer bounds, so add canvas or extra transparent space first if the bend needs room. Edit > Transform > Warp is usually easier for interactive bending; Shear is more useful when you need a repeatable, scriptable curve.

tools.name: Spherize
tools.description: Wraps the selection around a sphere, stretching the centre outward (positive amounts) or sucking it inward (negative amounts) with a spherical falloff. Unlike Pinch, the falloff follows a sphere's curvature, which makes it the better choice for mapping flat artwork onto a ball, a bubble or an eye. Horizontal Only and Vertical Only modes restrict the bulge to a cylinder in one axis.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: -100% to 100%. Positive bulges the selection outward, negative dishes it inward.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Normal (spherical in both axes), Horizontal Only or Vertical Only (cylindrical bulge in one axis).

tools.notes: Make a perfectly circular selection (Elliptical Marquee with Shift held) before applying, or the bulge will be elliptical. Applying the filter twice at 100% gives a stronger, more convincing sphere than one pass. Does not work on images larger than 11500 x 11500 pixels. Combine with a radial gradient on Multiply for shading to sell the 3D look.

tools.name: Twirl
tools.description: Rotates the selection around its centre, spinning the middle much more sharply than the edges so the image is drawn out into a spiral. A small angle gives a gentle swirl, large angles produce a tight vortex. Use it for whirlpool and galaxy effects, for abstract backgrounds, and (at very small angles) for adding a subtle sense of rotation to smoke and clouds.

parameters.name: Angle
parameters.description: Degrees of twist at the centre, -999 to 999. Positive twists clockwise, negative counter-clockwise; the falloff to zero is at the edge of the selection.

tools.example:
// Tight clockwise vortex
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.applyTwirl(360);   // angle, -999 to 999
tools.notes: The twirl is centred on the active selection's bounding box; with no selection it uses the whole layer. Feather the selection or the spiral ends abruptly at its boundary. Repeated moderate passes (Ctrl+F) look smoother than one extreme angle. Does not work on images larger than 11500 x 11500 pixels.

tools.name: Add Noise
tools.description: Sprinkles randomly valued pixels across the image to simulate film grain or sensor noise. Besides its obvious creative use, it is a practical repair tool: adding a little noise breaks up the banding that appears in gradients and feathered selections, and it restores believable texture to areas that have been over-retouched or cloned. Monochromatic mode keeps the noise neutral so only luminance, not colour, is disturbed.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: Noise strength as a percentage, 0.1 to 400.0.

parameters.name: Distribution
parameters.description: Uniform (random values evenly spread, subtle) or Gaussian (bell-curve distribution, more speckled and contrasty).

parameters.name: Monochromatic
parameters.description: When on, only tonal values are disturbed and the hue of each pixel is left alone - the right choice for film-grain simulation.

tools.notes: Add the noise on a separate 50% grey layer in Overlay or Soft Light mode so the grain amount stays adjustable via layer opacity. Adding noise before a heavy JPEG save is counterproductive - it inflates file size and gets crushed anyway. Supports 8-, 16- and 32-bit documents.

tools.name: Dust & Scratches
tools.description: Removes small defects by replacing pixels that differ sharply from their neighbours within a given radius. Radius sets how big a defect it can swallow and Threshold sets how different a pixel must be before it counts as a defect, so the pair is a trade-off between cleaning the image and destroying genuine detail. Use it on film scans, dusty negatives and old prints, ideally applied through a mask so only the damaged areas are affected.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Size in pixels of the area searched for dissimilar pixels, 1 to 16. Use the smallest value that still removes the specks.

parameters.name: Threshold
parameters.description: How different a pixel must be before it is eliminated, 0 to 255. Raising it protects genuine detail; 0 affects everything within the radius.

tools.example:
// Conservative dust removal on a scan
app.activeDocument.activeLayer.applyDustAndScratches(2, 20);   // radius 1-16, threshold 0-255
tools.notes: Always start with Threshold at 0, raise Radius until the defects vanish, then raise Threshold until the real detail returns - the reverse order gives worse results. Applied globally it softens the whole image; apply it on a duplicate layer with a black mask and paint white over the dust instead. Supports 8- and 16-bit documents.

tools.name: Median
tools.description: Replaces each pixel with the median brightness of its neighbours within the radius, discarding outliers instead of averaging them. Because the median is robust to extreme values, it removes speckle, hot pixels and motion artefacts while keeping edges much crisper than a Gaussian Blur of the same radius. At large radii it produces a distinctive plastic, posterised look often used as the smooth half of a frequency-separation retouch or for cartoon effects.

parameters.name: Radius
parameters.description: Radius in pixels of the neighbourhood searched for the median value; small values de-speckle, large values flatten the image into blobs.

tools.notes: Median is a good alternative to a blur when removing people or moving objects from a stack of exposures (Layer > Smart Objects > Stack Mode > Median does this across layers). Radii above roughly 10 start to eat fine detail irreversibly. Supports 8- and 16-bit documents.

tools.name: Reduce Noise
tools.description: Photoshop's dedicated noise-reduction dialog: it separates luminance noise from colour noise, preserves edge detail with its own Preserve Details control, adds back sharpening, and can remove JPEG compression artifacts. Advanced mode exposes per-channel strength and detail sliders so you can attack noise hardest in the blue channel, where it usually lives, without softening the green. Use it on high-ISO frames and rescued web JPEGs when a raw workflow is not available.

parameters.name: Strength
parameters.description: Amount of luminance noise reduction, 0 to 10.

parameters.name: Preserve Details
parameters.description: 0 to 100% - how much fine edge detail is protected from the smoothing.

parameters.name: Reduce Color Noise
parameters.description: 0 to 100% - removes the coloured speckles typical of high-ISO shadows.

parameters.name: Sharpen Details
parameters.description: 0 to 100% - re-sharpens after the smoothing pass.

parameters.name: Remove JPEG Artifact
parameters.description: Checkbox that targets the 8x8 blocking and ringing produced by heavy JPEG compression.

parameters.name: Advanced > Per Channel
parameters.description: Separate Strength and Preserve Details sliders for the Red, Green and Blue channels.

parameters.name: Settings
parameters.description: Save and load named presets from the dialog's settings menu.

tools.example:
1. Convert the layer with Filter > Convert for Smart Filters so the settings stay editable.
2. Choose Filter > Noise > Reduce Noise...
3. Set Reduce Color Noise first until the coloured speckles disappear (often 40-60%).
4. Raise Strength until luminance grain smooths out, then raise Preserve Details to bring edges back.
5. Switch to Advanced and push Strength higher on the Blue channel only.
6. Leave Sharpen Details at 0 and sharpen properly afterwards with Smart Sharpen.
tools.notes: Despeckle (Filter > Noise > Despeckle) is the one-click alternative in the same submenu: it detects edges and blurs everything except them, with no dialog and no options, which makes it handy for scanner moire but far cruder than Reduce Noise. For raw files, Camera Raw's Detail panel and the AI Denoise command give noticeably better results than this filter. Reduce Noise supports 8- and 16-bit documents. There is no ExtendScript DOM method for Reduce Noise, but applyDespeckle() exists for Despeckle.

tools.name: Pixelate
tools.description: A submenu of seven filters that clump pixels of similar colour into cells, producing halftone, mosaic, crystal and pointillist looks. They are used both creatively - retro print and comic effects, abstract backgrounds - and practically, since Mosaic is the standard way to censor a face, licence plate or document in a screenshot. All of them operate on the whole layer or the active selection.
tools.usage: Filter > Pixelate > Color Halftone... / Crystallize... / Mosaic... / Pointillize... / Mezzotint... / Facet / Fragment

parameters.name: Color Halftone
parameters.description: Simulates an enlarged halftone screen per channel: set Max Radius in pixels and a screen angle for each of channels 1-4.

parameters.name: Crystallize
parameters.description: Clumps pixels into solid-coloured polygons; a single Cell Size slider controls how big the crystals are.

parameters.name: Mosaic
parameters.description: Clumps pixels into square blocks of one colour; a single Cell Size slider. The standard pixelation/censoring filter.

parameters.name: Pointillize
parameters.description: Breaks the image into randomly placed dots over the current background colour; Cell Size sets the dot scale.

parameters.name: Mezzotint
parameters.description: Converts the image to a random pattern of black-and-white or fully saturated areas; choose a Type such as Fine Dots, Medium Dots, Grainy Dots, Coarse Dots, Short Lines, Medium Lines, Long Lines, Short Strokes, Medium Strokes or Long Strokes.

parameters.name: Facet
parameters.description: No dialog. Clumps similar colours into blocks of flat colour, giving a hand-painted or abstract-painting look. Apply repeatedly for a stronger effect.

parameters.name: Fragment
parameters.description: No dialog. Makes four offset copies of the selection and averages them, giving an out-of-register, shaken look.

tools.example:
1. To censor a face: select it with the Rectangular Marquee.
2. Choose Filter > Pixelate > Mosaic... and set Cell Size to about 1/10 of the selection's width.
3. Click OK and deselect.
4. For a retro print look instead, choose Filter > Pixelate > Color Halftone..., set Max Radius to 8 and leave the four screen angles at 108, 162, 90, 45.
5. Press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F) to reapply the last Pixelate filter with the same settings on another area.
tools.notes: Color Halftone and Mezzotint require an 8-bit document; Mosaic, Crystallize, Pointillize, Facet and Fragment also run in 16-bit. Pointillize fills the gaps between dots with the current background colour, so set that first. When pixelating for privacy, flatten and re-save - a Smart Filter can be switched off by anyone who receives the PSD. None of these have ExtendScript DOM methods; record an Action to batch them.

tools.name: Render
tools.description: A submenu of generators that create new image content rather than modifying what is already there: procedural clouds and fibres, a flame and tree generator that follow a path, a photographic lens flare, a full lighting-simulation dialog and an automatic picture frame. Because several of them replace the layer's pixels entirely, they are normally run on a new empty or filled layer and then blended in. Use them for skies, textures, atmospheric effects and studio-style relighting.
tools.usage: Filter > Render > Clouds / Difference Clouds / Fibers... / Flame... / Lens Flare... / Lighting Effects... / Picture Frame... / Tree...

parameters.name: Clouds
parameters.description: No dialog. Fills the layer with a soft random cloud pattern interpolated between the foreground and background colours; hold Alt/Opt while choosing it for a higher-contrast pattern. Replaces the layer's existing data.

parameters.name: Difference Clouds
parameters.description: No dialog. Generates the same pattern but blends it with the existing pixels using Difference mode; applying it repeatedly builds marble-like veining. Replaces the layer's existing data.

parameters.name: Fibers
parameters.description: Weaves the foreground and background colours into fibres. Variance controls colour spread (low = long streaks, high = short varied fibres), Strength controls the weave tightness, Randomize reseeds the pattern. Replaces the layer's existing data.

parameters.name: Flame
parameters.description: Renders flames along the currently selected work path. Basic tab: Flame Type (One Flame Along Path, Multiple Flames, Flame Along Path with various orientations), Length, Width, Angle, Interval, Adjust Interval for Loops, Quality. Advanced tab: Turbulent, Jag, Opacity, Flame Lines, Flame Bottom Alignment, Flame Style, Flame Shape, Randomize Shapes, Arrangement.

parameters.name: Lens Flare
parameters.description: Simulates light refracting inside a lens. Brightness 10-300%, a draggable flare centre, and Lens Type: 50-300mm Zoom, 35mm Prime, 105mm Prime or Movie Prime.

parameters.name: Lighting Effects
parameters.description: A full relighting workspace with on-canvas widgets. Light types Spot, Point and Infinite; per-light Colour, Intensity, Hotspot, and global Colorize, Exposure, Gloss, Metallic, Ambience and a Texture channel with Height for bump mapping. Presets can be saved and loaded.

parameters.name: Picture Frame
parameters.description: Draws a decorative frame around the image or selection; choose a frame style and adjust its size, colour and pattern options. Implemented as a scripted (Generator-based) filter.

parameters.name: Tree
parameters.description: Generates a tree along the selected work path. Base Tree Type plus Light Direction, Leaves Amount, Leaves Size, Branches Height, Branches Thickness, Default Leaves, Randomize Shapes, Arrangement, Rotate Leaves, Camera Tilt and flat-shading options.

tools.example:
1. Add a new empty layer (Ctrl+Shift+N).
2. Set the foreground to a sky blue and the background to white, then choose Filter > Render > Clouds.
3. Set the layer to Screen and lower its opacity for a soft haze.
4. For a flare: select a filled pixel layer, choose Filter > Render > Lens Flare..., drag the crosshair over a bright area, set Brightness to 120% and Lens Type to 105mm Prime.
5. For flames or a tree: draw a path with the Pen tool first, keep it selected in the Paths panel, then choose Filter > Render > Flame... or Tree...
tools.notes: Lighting Effects, Flame, Picture Frame and Tree all require an 8-bit/channel RGB document AND Use Graphics Processor enabled in Preferences > Performance - they are greyed out otherwise. Clouds, Difference Clouds and Fibers overwrite the active layer's pixels, so always run them on a new or duplicated layer. Flame and Tree need a work path selected in the Paths panel or the command reports that no path exists. Lens Flare cannot be applied to an empty/transparent layer - fill it with black and set the layer to Screen instead. ExtendScript offers applyLensFlare(brightness, flareCenter, lensType), applyClouds() and applyDifferenceClouds() but nothing for Flame, Tree, Picture Frame or Lighting Effects.

tools.name: Sharpen
tools.description: The submenu that increases the contrast of adjacent pixels to make an image read as crisper. Unsharp Mask is the classic, predictable three-slider sharpener; Smart Sharpen is the modern one, with a choice of blur model, separate Shadows and Highlights fade controls and better halo suppression. Sharpen, Sharpen More and Sharpen Edges are one-click versions with no dialog. Always sharpen last, at output size, and preferably through a mask or Smart Filter.
tools.usage: Filter > Sharpen > Unsharp Mask... / Smart Sharpen... / Sharpen / Sharpen More / Sharpen Edges

parameters.name: Unsharp Mask > Amount
parameters.description: Strength of the edge contrast boost, 1 to 500%. Typical screen output uses 60-150%.

parameters.name: Unsharp Mask > Radius
parameters.description: How far from an edge the contrast is altered, 0.1 to 250.0 pixels. Small radii (0.5-1.5) sharpen fine detail; large radii add local contrast.

parameters.name: Unsharp Mask > Threshold
parameters.description: How different neighbouring pixels must be before they are sharpened, 0 to 255. Raise it to 3-10 to stop sharpening skin and sky noise.

parameters.name: Smart Sharpen > Amount / Radius
parameters.description: Same meaning as in Unsharp Mask, but with a better anti-halo algorithm.

parameters.name: Smart Sharpen > Reduce Noise
parameters.description: 0 to 100% - suppresses the noise that sharpening would otherwise amplify.

parameters.name: Smart Sharpen > Remove
parameters.description: The blur model to invert: Gaussian Blur (Unsharp Mask equivalent), Lens Blur (best for photographic detail, fewest halos) or Motion Blur (with an Angle dial, for directional camera shake).

parameters.name: Smart Sharpen > Shadows / Highlights tabs
parameters.description: Fade Amount, Tonal Width and Radius for each end of the tonal range, so you can pull sharpening out of dark or blown areas independently.

parameters.name: Sharpen
parameters.description: No dialog. A fixed, mild sharpening pass over the whole selection.

parameters.name: Sharpen More
parameters.description: No dialog. Roughly three to four times stronger than Sharpen.

parameters.name: Sharpen Edges
parameters.description: No dialog. Finds the areas of significant colour change and sharpens only those, leaving flat areas smooth.

parameters.name: Shake Reduction
parameters.description: Removed from Photoshop in the April 2022 release (version 23.3) because the technology was incompatible with newer development platforms - it is NOT present in Photoshop 2025 (v26). Use Smart Sharpen with Remove: Motion Blur, or Camera Raw's Enhance, for camera-shake blur instead.

tools.notes: Sharpen at 100% zoom or you will over-sharpen. Convert the layer to a Smart Object first so the sharpening can be re-tuned and masked, and set the Smart Filter blend mode to Luminosity to avoid colour fringing.
