Do the sharpening after resizing to final output dimensions. Unsharp Mask and Smart Sharpen support 8- and 16-bit documents. Shake Reduction no longer exists - see the parameter note above.

tools.name: Stylize
tools.description: A submenu that displaces pixels and boosts contrast to produce impressionistic, embossed, edge-traced and painterly effects. Find Edges and Trace Contour turn a photograph into a line drawing, Emboss and Extrude add relief, Oil Paint applies a full brush-simulation engine, and Wind, Tiles, Diffuse and Solarize give motion, fragmentation, grain and darkroom effects. Use them for illustration, texture generation and stylised title treatments.
tools.usage: Filter > Stylize > Diffuse... / Emboss... / Extrude... / Find Edges / Oil Paint... / Solarize / Tiles... / Trace Contour... / Wind...

parameters.name: Diffuse
parameters.description: Shuffles pixels within a small neighbourhood to soften focus. Modes: Normal, Darken Only, Lighten Only, Anisotropic (which follows edge direction and gives a smeared, painterly look).

parameters.name: Emboss
parameters.description: Turns the image grey and traces edges with the original colour so it looks stamped. Angle (-360 to 360), Height in pixels, and Amount 1-500%.

parameters.name: Extrude
parameters.description: Gives a 3D texture of Blocks or Pyramids. Size and Depth (Random or Level-based), plus Solid Front Faces and Mask Incomplete Blocks options.

parameters.name: Find Edges
parameters.description: No dialog. Outlines the areas of significant transition with dark lines on a white background - the fastest route to a sketch look.

parameters.name: Oil Paint
parameters.description: Brush-simulation engine with Stylization, Cleanliness, Scale and Bristle Detail sliders, plus Lighting controls for Angular Direction and Shine. Requires the GPU.

parameters.name: Solarize
parameters.description: No dialog. Blends a negative and a positive of the image, reproducing the darkroom Sabattier effect.

parameters.name: Tiles
parameters.description: Breaks the image into offset square tiles. Number Of Tiles, Maximum Offset percentage, and what fills the gaps: Background Color, Foreground Color, Inverse Image or Unaltered Image.

parameters.name: Trace Contour
parameters.description: Finds the major brightness transitions and outlines them thinly per channel. Level 0-255 sets the brightness to trace, and Edge selects Lower or Upper.

parameters.name: Wind
parameters.description: Adds small horizontal streaks for a windblown look. Method: Wind, Blast or Stagger; Direction: From The Right or From The Left.

tools.example:
1. Duplicate the layer (Ctrl+J) so the original survives.
2. Choose Filter > Stylize > Find Edges for an instant line drawing, then Image > Adjustments > Desaturate.
3. Set the layer's blend mode to Multiply over the original for a sketched-photo hybrid.
4. For a relief instead: Filter > Stylize > Emboss..., Angle 135, Height 3 px, Amount 120%, then set the layer to Overlay to keep the underlying colour.
5. For wind streaks: rotate the layer 90 degrees, apply Filter > Stylize > Wind... (Method: Blast), and rotate back - Wind only works horizontally.
tools.notes: Oil Paint requires an 8-bit RGB document and Use Graphics Processor enabled in Preferences > Performance. Wind only streaks horizontally, so rotate the layer to get a vertical effect. Find Edges, Solarize and Diffuse have no dialog and therefore no settings to fade from within the filter - use Edit > Fade immediately afterwards, or a Smart Filter's blending options. Glowing Edges belongs to the same family but lives inside Filter Gallery, not this submenu. None of these have dedicated ExtendScript DOM methods.

tools.name: Other
tools.description: A catch-all submenu of technical utilities rather than creative effects: a user-programmable convolution kernel, an edge-isolating high-pass, morphological spread and choke operators for masks, a pixel-shifting offset for building seamless tiles, and a channel-remapping HSB/HSL converter. These are the filters that underpin sharpening, masking and texture-tiling workflows. Learn High Pass and Offset first - they come up constantly in production work.
tools.usage: Filter > Other > High Pass... / Custom... / Maximum... / Minimum... / Offset... / HSB/HSL

parameters.name: High Pass
parameters.description: Keeps only the detail within the given Radius where sharp colour transitions occur and flattens everything else to mid-grey (a radius of 0.1 px keeps only edge pixels). The exact inverse of Gaussian Blur, and the basis of high-pass sharpening and frequency separation.

parameters.name: Custom
parameters.description: A 5x5 convolution kernel you fill in yourself, plus Scale (the divisor applied to the sum of the weighted brightnesses) and Offset (added to the scaled result). Custom kernels can be saved to disk and reloaded.

parameters.name: Maximum
parameters.description: Morphological dilate: spreads white and chokes black within the Radius, with a Preserve setting of Squareness or Roundness. Used to grow a mask or a matte.

parameters.name: Minimum
parameters.description: Morphological erode: spreads black and chokes white within the Radius, with the same Squareness/Roundness Preserve option. Used to shrink a mask and pull a halo off a cut-out edge.

parameters.name: Offset
parameters.description: Shifts the layer by Horizontal and Vertical pixel amounts (-6144 to 6144) and fills the vacated area according to Undefined Areas: Set To Background, Repeat Edge Pixels or Wrap Around. Wrap Around is how seamless tiles are built.

parameters.name: HSB/HSL
parameters.description: Remaps the RGB channels into Hue/Saturation/Brightness or Hue/Saturation/Lightness triplets (and back), by choosing an input Row Order and an output Row Order. Lets you run ordinary RGB filters on what are effectively the H, S and B channels.

tools.notes: High Pass leaves the layer mid-grey, so it is only useful with a contrast blend mode (Overlay, Soft Light or Hard Light) or as the high-frequency half of a frequency separation. Maximum and Minimum are usually applied to a layer mask or alpha channel rather than to image pixels - target the mask thumbnail first. Offset with Wrap Around only produces a seamless tile if you then heal the cross-shaped seam it exposes in the middle. applyCustomFilter takes exactly 25 values, in left-to-right, top-to-bottom order matching the Custom dialog grid. High Pass, Maximum, Minimum and Offset support 8- and 16-bit documents; HSB/HSL is 8-bit RGB only.
